text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Opposition wins no-confidence vote, 49-44, but government remains for lack of a 61-vote majority in 120-seat Knesset.
- Labour party leader Ehud Barak holds "emergency meeting" with Jordan's King Hussein.
- Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh to U.S. on peace mission; Foreign Minister David Levy to meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in Brussels.
- Treasury requests 90 million shekel transfer to West Bank Jewish settlers from Immigration and Absorption Ministry.
- Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman unveils 800 million shekel extra budget cut tonight. Defence and health ministers demand one-billion-shekel-plus increase.
- Magic Software Enterprises to launch cutback plan, company develops software tools.
- Currency liberalisation measures take effect this week.
- Israel Aircraft Industires in $120 million bid to sell satellite to Vietnam.
- Tel Aviv's Ben-Gurion Airport traffic rises 13 percent during May-June.
GLOBES
- Even after an 800-million-shekel budget cut -- the deficit will deviate about 0.3 percent from the target.
- Koor buyers ask to buy double the number of shares but refuse to raise the price. Share price rose 6 percent.
HAARETZ
- United States warns: We'll pull our hand out of the Middle East peace negotiations. Washington considers cancelling economic conference in Qatar scheduled for November.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- U.S. initiative for reviving talks: Israel slows down construction of Jewish settlements and Palestinians agree to accelerate final-status negotiations.
- "The foreign investor in Koor -- pension fund of General Electric".
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman stays at Eilat hotel at price 35 percent below that of a regular customer. He says nothing wrong --it was a group rate.
- After a 10-year ban the Uzi returns to shops in the United States.
MAARIV
- Attorney Yitzhak Molho, special Israeli envoy, secretly met Arafat: "Netanyahu wants to renew the negotiations".
- Assessment: General Electric funds stand behind purchase of Israel's Koor.
